listeningScripts.title: Airline Baggage Delay
listeningScripts.text: Passenger: Excuse me, my baggage didn't arrive on my flight from Vancouver. Airline Agent: I'm very sorry to hear that. Let me help you file a report. What is your confirmation number? Passenger: It's VH-4829. I arrived about an hour ago on flight AC-127. Agent: Got it. Did you check your bag through to your final destination or pick it up here in Calgary? Passenger: I checked it all the way to Calgary. I have the baggage claim ticket right here. Agent: Perfect. Can I see that? The tag number is LM-58493. Your bag is a black Samsonite roller, correct? Passenger: Yes, that's right. It has a red ribbon on the handle. Agent: Great. I've found it in the system. It actually came off the plane but was misrouted to Edmonton by mistake. It's on the next flight back to Calgary, which arrives at 6:15 PM tonight. Passenger: So I'll have it this evening? Agent: Yes, we'll have it delivered to your hotel by 8 PM. Where are you staying? Passenger: The Fairmont Palliser downtown. What compensation will I get? Agent: Because the delay is less than 24 hours and the bag will be delivered today, we'll provide a $50 travel voucher for your next flight with us.

listeningScripts.title: Music Concert Plans
listeningScripts.text: Alex: Are you going to the concert next Saturday? Casey: Which one? There are a few shows next weekend. Alex: The indie rock festival at the waterfront. Casey: Oh yeah, I've been thinking about it. How much are tickets? Alex: They're forty dollars each. Casey: That's not too bad. Who's performing? Alex: Five bands. The headliner is The Northern Stars. Casey: Oh, I love them. What time does it start? Alex: Six PM. It should wrap up around eleven. Casey: That's pretty late. Is there parking nearby? Alex: Yeah, there's a parking lot right by the venue. It's five dollars for the whole night. Casey: That's reasonable. Should we get food there or bring our own? Alex: They have food vendors there, but it's probably expensive. Casey: Let's grab something before we go then. Alex: Good idea. Want me to buy your ticket? Casey: Yeah, that would be great. Just send me the bill.

listeningScripts.title: Hospital Visitor Guidelines
listeningScripts.text: Welcome to City Hospital. We're glad you're visiting someone here. Please review our visitor guidelines for patient safety and comfort. Visiting hours are 10 AM to 8 PM daily. Each patient can have a maximum of two visitors at a time in their room. This ensures proper rest and medical care. Children under twelve must be accompanied by an adult. We restrict visits from children with colds or contagious illnesses. Visitors should wash their hands upon arrival and before leaving. Hand-sanitizer stations are located throughout the facility. Quiet voices are required in patient rooms and hallways. Please avoid using cell phones in patient areas. Photography is not permitted without the patient's written consent. Flowers and plants are welcome, but balloons are not allowed due to interference with medical equipment. Food brought from outside is permitted only if approved by nursing staff. Many patients have dietary restrictions. Visiting a patient receiving isolation care requires special precautions. Nursing staff will provide instructions. Do not disturb patients' medical equipment, monitors, or IV lines. Visitors with concerns should speak to staff at the nursing station. Parking is available in the north lot at five dollars per visit. An elevator is located near the main entrance for easy access.

listeningScripts.title: Alberta Heritage Museum Expansion
listeningScripts.text: The Alberta Heritage Museum is embarking on a 95 million dollar expansion project that will double its exhibition space. The project, spanning five years, will create new galleries dedicated to Indigenous history, early settlement, and contemporary Alberta culture. Museum Director Patricia Wong announced that the expansion will feature interactive exhibits and state-of-the-art multimedia installations. The project will generate approximately 600 construction jobs over the expansion period. Funding comes from government grants, private donations, and corporate sponsorships. The museum currently attracts 480,000 visitors annually, and officials project this will increase by 45 percent following the expansion. A new 2,000-square-meter research and conservation facility will support artifact preservation. Four new galleries will be built, including a dedicated space for rotating temporary exhibitions. Community consultation has identified strong public support, with 78 percent of surveyed Albertans favoring the project. The expansion is scheduled to be completed by 2031.

listeningScripts.title: Local Food System Development
listeningScripts.text:
Farmer Cooperative Director Maria: We're launching an initiative to build a more resilient local food system for our region. Currently, about 87 percent of our food is imported from outside the province. We want to increase local food production and support our farmers. We're proposing a farmers market expansion and direct-to-consumer delivery programs. The cooperative will help coordinate logistics and marketing.

Grocery Store Manager Paul: I understand the value of local food, Maria, but I'm concerned about pricing and consistency. Local producers can't always compete with the prices we get from large distributors. And seasonality is an issue—in winter, local farmers have limited options. My customers expect year-round availability and competitive pricing.

Public Health Officer Dr. Sarah: Actually, Paul, local food systems have documented health benefits. Communities with stronger local food networks show 22 percent higher rates of fresh produce consumption. Plus, reducing transportation distance improves food safety and nutrition because products reach consumers fresher. And we should consider the long-term economic impact. Local spending circulates within the community.

Small Farm Owner James: I'd love to participate in this initiative. Currently, I sell about 40 percent of my production to the farmers market, but I'd like to do more direct sales. The issue is I don't have the infrastructure for packaging and distribution. If the cooperative could help with that, I could increase production by 60 percent.

listeningScripts.title: Climate Migration and Urban Planning
listeningScripts.text: Climate change is already forcing large-scale human migration, and we need to prepare for it now. Rising sea levels, extreme weather, and changing precipitation patterns are making entire regions uninhabitable. We're not just talking about future problems—this is happening today. Small island nations are literally disappearing. Coastal cities are experiencing increased flooding. Agricultural regions are becoming deserts. Where will these people go? History shows us that unplanned migration creates chaos: overcrowded cities, slums, resource conflicts, and instability. I believe cities and countries need to proactively plan for climate migration. This means developing infrastructure and housing in climate-resilient areas, creating economic opportunities for migrants, and managing population flows thoughtfully. Canada and the northern regions of other countries will likely become more desirable as climate conditions shift. Rather than letting this happen chaotically, we should be designing inclusive urban expansion, building climate-resilient communities, and preparing labor markets for population shifts. Some people see climate migration as a negative, but it's inevitable. The real question is whether we manage it responsibly or let it cause humanitarian crises. I'm advocating for proactive planning now. We should be expanding housing, infrastructure, and economic capacity in climate-safe regions. We should also help other countries adapt in place where possible. But denying this reality and refusing to plan is irresponsible.
